title: Disconnect live frontend from Kissinger: cut Postgres-only where parity exists, flag remaining touchpoints
description:
Drew: 'Do not remove kissinger, but remove the dual write so it is disconnected from the actual lived performance of the frontend. We want to be able to use the system as though that interface is built entirely on postgres. We will worry about graph operations later.'

Kissinger integration/CLI/API must stay. Only the LIVE request path changes.

Scope (verified by reading every live-path Kissinger call site):

REMOVE Kissinger call, Postgres becomes sole write/read (parity already verified in GH #44/#45/#46, dual-write was only back-compat instrumentation):
- POST /api/contacts/create, /api/contacts/bulk-create — self-mint id instead of Kissinger assignEntity
- PATCH /api/contacts/[id]/notes
- DELETE /api/contacts/[id]/remove-prospect
- GET+POST /api/contacts/[id]/events — rebuild GET from Postgres ContactEvent (feeds ContactEventsTab + TrigifySignalsTab)
- PATCH /api/contacts/[id]/stage (funnel stage)
- POST /api/investors/pipeline-stage
- GET /api/contacts/[id]/score — reuse fetchContactDetailFromPostgres + scoreContact (pattern already built for contacts/[id]/page.tsx)
- Homepage stats widget (src/app/(main)/page.tsx, fetchKissingerFunnelData) — new Postgres aggregate-count module, no graph traversal needed
- POST /api/booking/create Kissinger fire-and-forget sync (syncBookingToKissinger) — Booking already fully Postgres; Kissinger sync was pure mirroring

LEAVE ON KISSINGER, FLAG TO DREW (not graph ops, but genuinely blocked / out of easy-cutover scope, distinct from the one exception Drew named):
1. /api/contacts/[id]/intro-path — Drew's named exception (graph traversal / recursive CTE not built).
2. Outreach subsystem (new-batch, skip, outreach-touch, outreach-response, generate-message, bulk-generate, reload-tasks, feedback, signals/dismiss, signals/snooze, outreach/page.tsx reads) — read-path cutover explicitly gated in GH #43/outreach-queue-read.ts on a documented data-completeness gap (only ~25% of active queue rows have resolvable Organization, ~62% have title). Cutting over now would blank company/title for most real rows — a known, previously-rejected regression. Not a graph problem, but not safe to flip without Drew's call.
3. Contacts page 'All' tab + entity search box (searchKissinger) — Kissinger's ranked cross-entity search (entities + interaction snippets) has no Postgres equivalent; 'All' tab was explicitly out of scope in GH #44. Left as a second/third gap alongside Outreach.

OUT OF SCOPE (dead code, not exercised by any live caller — verified via grep across src/components and src/app, left untouched, no live risk):
- GET /api/contacts/[id]/detail (only caller: orphaned ContactDetailPanel.tsx, not imported anywhere)
- GET /api/prospects/[id]/score (no caller found anywhere)
- POST /api/contacts/[id]/contacted (no caller found in this app or the eloso-linkedin-extension sidepanel)

Do NOT touch: kissinger.ts itself, the Kissinger project/CLI/API, or any backfill/migration script.
acceptance_criteria: All 9 listed live-path mutation/read routes call Postgres only, with unit tests proving Kissinger is never invoked (mock throws on call) and the route still succeeds. Existing dual-write tests updated to reflect single-write. Manual verification with KISSINGER_API_URL pointed at an unreachable host confirms contacts/investors/funnel/events/booking flows still work end-to-end. PR opened documenting the 3 flagged remaining touchpoints for Drew's decision.
notes: PR opened: https://github.com/eloso-bisque/eloso-bisque/pull/53 (branch feature/kissinger-dualwrite-removal). Implemented per the plan in this issue's description: 9 mutation/read routes cut over to Postgres-only, homepage stats rebuilt on Postgres, booking Kissinger fire-and-forget sync removed, Trigify signals split into its own still-Kissinger-backed route to avoid silently blanking the Signals tab. 3 known touchpoints left flagged for Drew (intro-path, Outreach subsystem, Contacts All-tab+search) plus 3 confirmed-dead routes left untouched. Full test suite green against pre-existing baseline (11 pre-existing failures unrelated, verified via git stash). Manual verification against real prod Postgres with Kissinger pointed at an unreachable host, plus one reversible write test on a synthetic fixture contact. Not closing — awaiting review.
close_reason: PR #53 merged (11b5866) and deployed to production (https://eloso-bisque-virid.vercel.app). Homepage stat cards, contact detail, and events routes verified live against prod Postgres. 3 flagged touchpoints (intro-path, Outreach, Contacts All-tab+search) remain on Kissinger pending Drew's decision.

title: Prisma Phase 2/3: Kissinger migration script + dual-write
description:
Database is now live (Neon via Vercel integration, eloso-bisque-prod, migration 20260721194352_init applied — all 16+ models created and confirmed reachable from production).

Remaining per docs/prisma-schema-design.md section 4.1:

Phase 2: One-time Node.js script to backfill all existing Kissinger GraphQL entities into the new Postgres schema (Contact, Organization, RelationshipFrom, OutreachQueueEntry, GeneratedMessage, Signal, ContactEvent, etc. per the mapping table in docs/prisma-schema-design.md section 4.2). Nothing has been migrated from Kissinger yet — the new DB currently has empty tables.

Phase 3: Dual-write period. Mutation API routes need to write to both Kissinger (back-compat) and Postgres. Read paths migrate in this order:
1. Activity Dashboard -> ActivityLog queries (simplest, do first)
2. Outreach queue -> OutreachQueueEntry + OutreachTouch
3. Contacts listing
4. Sectors heatmap (with Contacts listing)
5. Investors section
6. Contact detail / Funnel Kanban (last, needs relationship data fully populated)

Phase 4 (later): cut over, decommission Kissinger once dual-write is stable 2+ weeks.

No code for phases 2-4 has been written yet — this is scoping/tracking only.
notes:
[2026-07-22] Phase 3.1 (GH #42, Activity Dashboard dual-write + read cutover) implemented, tested, and deployed to prod. PR: https://github.com/eloso-bisque/eloso-bisque/pull/47

- Dual-write live in src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts and src/app/api/contacts/[id]/outreach-touch/route.ts (ActivityLog rows alongside untouched KV writes).
- src/lib/prisma.ts fixed (Prisma 7 needs an explicit driver adapter - was previously unused/unbuilt).
- Historical KV data seeded into ActivityLog and read-path cutover deployed to https://eloso-bisque-virid.vercel.app/admin/activity.
- Parity verified against real prod data: 42/42 rows matched (all 3 users, daily + last_login + all-time outreach totals).
- Issue #41 (Kissinger backfill, seeds the 3 User rows) landed mid-session, unblocking real verification instead of synthetic fixtures.
- Known gap: no real browser login test (no test credentials for drew/ben/jake) - flagged in the PR for a human to spot-check post-merge.

Not closing this bd issue - Phase 3.2-3.6 (Outreach queue, Contacts listing, Sectors heatmap, Investors, Contact detail/Funnel Kanban) remain, tracked as GH #43-#46.
[Phase 2 progress] Kissinger -> Postgres backfill complete: PR #49 (eloso-bisque/eloso-bisque), GH issue #41 updated.

Ran the real backfill script against production Kissinger + production Neon Postgres (eloso-bisque-prod). Final counts: Organization 5846/5846 (exact match to Kissinger's live org count), Contact 9234+/9234+ (exact match at time of run; Kissinger under continuous unrelated live write load so the exact figure drifts -- backfill is idempotent/safely re-runnable to pick up drift), RelationshipFrom 14887, OutreachQueueEntry 1061, GeneratedMessage 152, Signal 686, ContactEvent 262, User 3, Sector 12. 10471 edges of relation types with no RelationType enum value (may_know/buys_from/supplies_to/contract_mfg_for) correctly skipped and counted, not force-mapped.

Manual record diffs (Erle Shepard contact, Denver Ventures org) confirmed field-level correctness against Kissinger source. Idempotency verified via repeated small-scope runs (identical counts on re-run).

Phase 3 (dual-write + read-path migration, GH #42-46) and Phase 4 (decommission) remain, tracked separately per the existing implementation plan comment on this issue. Not closing this issue -- leaving open until Phase 3/4 land.
[2026-07-22] Bug fix on top of PR #48 (GH #43, Phase 3.2 Outreach queue dual-write): independent review flagged that OutreachQueueEntry's `@@unique([contactId, isActive])` over-constrained inactive (history) rows to one per contact, not just active ones (isActive is NOT NULL, so a plain unique index caps both values). Any contact deactivated twice (e.g. assign -> sent -> reassign -> skip) silently lost its second deactivation write, since every dualWrite* function follows the never-throw/log-and-swallow contract.

Fix: migration 20260722114253_fix_outreach_queue_partial_unique_active_assignment replaces the full unique index with a partial one (`CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... WHERE "isActive" = true`), hand-authored since Prisma's schema DSL can't express partial indexes. Verified empirically against prod before applying: 0 contacts had 2+ active rows (no conflict risk). Applied via `prisma migrate deploy` against prod (eloso-bisque-prod / Neon) -- confirmed `prisma migrate status`/`migrate diff` show no drift.

New integration test (src/lib/__tests__/integration/outreach-queue-second-deactivation-integration.test.ts, opt-in via RUN_INTEGRATION=true, real Postgres, synthetic BulkTest fixture only) drives the exact two-deactivation cycle and queries rows back. Confirmed it fails against the old migration and passes against the new one (falsifiability proof run against a disposable local scratch Postgres, not prod).

Also reconciled the 411 vs 990 active-row-count discrepancy PR #48's reviewer flagged (see comment added to src/lib/outreach-queue-read.ts) -- both counts are real, from the same query, ~50 min apart on 2026-07-22, while the GH #41 backfill was still populating rows (411 assigned in the 10:00 UTC hour, 579 more in the 11:00 UTC hour).

Pushed as new commits on the existing feature/issue-43-outreach-queue-dual-write branch, updating PR #48 in place (not self-merging -- awaiting independent review).
[2026-07-30] Closed as superseded. PR #53 (feature/kissinger-dualwrite-removal, merged 2026-07-26) cut the live frontend over to Postgres-only reads/writes for all parity-verified CRUD paths, superseding this tracking issue's Phase 2-4 scope. Phase 2 backfill (scripts/backfill-kissinger.ts) and Phase 3 dual-write completed across GH #42-#46 before #53 landed. Remaining scoped-out items (Outreach queue read cutover pending org/title backfill completeness, OutreachFeedback schema, Contacts full-text search, intro-path) tracked separately per Stage-1 review 2026-07-30.

comments.author: Lobster
comments.text:
Implementation plan (orchestrated via functional-engineer subagents, one GitHub issue per phase, sequential due to shared dual-write infra dependencies):

1. GH #41 - Backfill script (Phase 2): one-time Node/TS script, Kissinger GraphQL -> Postgres, idempotent/upsert on kissingerId, seeds 3 Users.
2. GH #42 - Dual-write infra (Prisma client) + Activity Dashboard read migration (Phase 3.1).
3. GH #43 - Outreach queue dual-write + read migration (Phase 3.2).
4. GH #44 - Contacts listing + Sectors heatmap read migration (Phase 3.3/3.4).
5. GH #45 - Investors section read migration (Phase 3.5).
6. GH #46 - Contact detail / Funnel Kanban read migration (Phase 3.6, last).

Phase 4 (Kissinger decommission) explicitly NOT in this pass - requires 2+ weeks of stable dual-write observation per bd issue description. Will recommend a dated follow-up.

Each issue goes through functional-engineer (Opus): branch + Docker dev + TDD + PR, with manual proof-of-work required. After each PR merges, deploying via vercel --prod and verifying prod before starting the next phase (phases build on shared dual-write code, so sequenced not parallelized).

comments.author: Lobster
comments.text:
[2026-07-22] Phase 3.2 (GH #43, Outreach queue dual-write) implemented, tested, and PR opened: https://github.com/eloso-bisque/eloso-bisque/pull/48

- Dual-write added for all 6 in-scope mutation routes (new-batch, skip, outreach-touch, outreach-response, generate-message, bulk-generate) -> OutreachQueueEntry/OutreachTouch/OutreachResponse/GeneratedMessage. unique_active_assignment invariant enforced at the app layer (deactivate-then-create in one transaction), TDD'd with a falsifiability check.
- Found + fixed a pre-existing production bug while manual-testing: recordOutreachResponse (src/lib/kissinger.ts) passed the app's ResponseType casing straight through to Kissinger's GraphQL enum, which expects SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. Every real "Log Response" call was failing silently. Fixed + unit tested.
- Read-path cutover (fetchProspectContacts/fetchSentContacts -> Postgres) is NOT done: verified live against prod that only ~25% of active queue entries have a resolvable Organization and ~62% have a title (RelationshipFrom has only 15 rows total across 500 backfilled Contacts). Cutting over now would blank company/title for most real users. Built + unit-tested the Postgres read functions (src/lib/outreach-queue-read.ts) and a gating script (scripts/verify-outreach-parity.ts) but left them un-wired pending a completed GH #41 backfill (org-linking + title extraction).
- IMPORTANT: GH #41 (Kissinger backfill) is NOT actually merged despite earlier notes here saying so - gh issue view 41 shows it open, no PR. The ~500 Contact/Organization rows and ~990 OutreachQueueEntry rows already live in prod Postgres came from an uncommitted local script run, never reviewed. Verified structurally sound (no invariant violations, spot-checked against live Kissinger) but incomplete (see above). Recommend retroactively writing up and landing GH #41's real backfill script before GH #44 (Contacts listing) proceeds, since that read migration will hit the same completeness gap.
- Not touched: outreach/feedback (no dedicated Postgres model in scope, would require a schema.prisma change) and outreach/reload-tasks (operates on the global candidate pool, orthogonal to per-user OutreachQueueEntry assignment) - reasoning in the PR.

Not closing this bd issue - Phase 3.3-3.6 (GH #44-46) and Phase 4 remain. GH #44 should account for the GH #41 completeness gap flagged here.

comments.author: Lobster
comments.text:
[2026-07-22] Phase 3.3/3.4 (GH #44, Contacts listing + Sectors heatmap) implemented, tested, PR opened: https://github.com/eloso-bisque/eloso-bisque/pull/50

- Contacts listing (People/VC/Prospects/Other-Orgs tabs) cut over to typed-field Postgres queries. Verified exact parity against live Kissinger for org segments (vc=189, prospects=38, other-orgs=5619, all 5,846 orgs) and near-exact for people (9204 vs 9219, explained by Kissinger's continuous live write load).
- Sectors heatmap cut over too, but only after confirming completeness: just 23 of 5,846 orgs (0.4%) have any sector assigned, identically in both Kissinger and Postgres -- pre-existing business-data sparsity, not a migration gap, so this is a lateral move not a regression. Seeded Sector.defaultAssignee for 9 of 12 sectors from SECTOR_PREFERENCE (additive, dry-run verified, idempotent); left 3 ambiguous sectors (ev/chemicals/aerospace) unmapped rather than guessing a teammate assignment.
- Found and fixed a real display bug: heatmap ICP color/label helpers assumed a 0-1 fraction (Kissinger's avgIcpScore was always null in prod, so this was never exercised); Postgres icpScore is 0-100 like everywhere else in the app. Would have rendered "7800%" without the fix.
- Closed the dual-write gap #43 flagged: 5 of 7 in-scope contact mutation routes (create, bulk-create, notes, remove-prospect, events) had zero Postgres dual-write. Added it, following the established never-throw contract. enrich (delegates out-of-process) and score (read-only) reviewed and left untouched.
- Also fixed a pre-existing `next build` break in scripts/backfill-kissinger.ts caused by #48's partial-unique-index fix (Prisma no longer generates the `unique_active_assignment` compound-unique type) -- this issue's own DoD requires a working `vercel --prod` deploy, so had to unblock it.
- Manual test: built + ran the app locally against real prod Postgres/Kissinger (read-only, via the existing X-Internal-Secret bypass) and confirmed real data renders correctly on /sectors, /sectors/[slug], and all 4 /contacts segments. Also caught /sectors being statically prerendered (no dynamic signal from Prisma reads) and added force-dynamic, matching the #47 precedent.

Not self-merging -- awaiting independent review per the pattern on #47/#48/#49. Not closing this bd issue -- Phase 3.5/3.6 (GH #45/#46, Investors + Contact detail/Funnel Kanban) and Phase 4 (decommission) remain.

title: Clean up 125 pre-existing duplicate-email Contact groups
description:
2026-07-30 audit (during a Prisma schema completeness review requested by
Drew) found 125 groups of Contact rows sharing the same case-insensitive
email (250 rows total) already in production Postgres. Spot-checked several
groups (e.g. two "Ashley Carter" / acarter@sig.org rows, two "Bruce
Baumgartner" / bruce@zoox.com rows) — confirmed genuine duplicates, not a
shared-inbox coincidence: identical name, identical email, different
kissingerId, both created within ~1 second of each other, both noted "Added
from SIG Webinar June 2026 enrichment list" — looks like an import/enrichment
batch that ran twice or double-inserted.

Not fixed as part of the schema-completeness pass because merging duplicates
requires human judgment (which record is canonical, e.g. which one has
outreach history attached — OutreachQueueEntry/OutreachTouch/ContactEvent
rows keyed to a duplicate's id would need to be reassigned or the merge
would lose history) and isn't safe to automate blindly.

Forward-looking half already fixed: src/lib/contacts-dual-write.ts's
findDuplicateContactByEmail is now wired into both
POST /api/contacts/create and POST /api/contacts/bulk-create, rejecting new
duplicates at create time. This issue is just for the pre-existing 250 rows.

Suggested approach: for each of the 125 groups, pick the row with richer
history (more ContactEvent/OutreachTouch/OutreachResponse rows, or the
earlier createdAt as tiebreaker), reassign any FK references from the loser
row to the winner, then delete the loser. Query to re-find the groups:
  SELECT lower(email), count(*) FROM "Contact"
  WHERE email IS NOT NULL AND email != ''
  GROUP BY lower(email) HAVING count(*) > 1;
